question.value: Establish the molecular gas distribution, star formation efficiency, dynamics, and star formation triggers of intermediate-redshift (0.28 < z < 0.44) U/LIRGs located in the transition region between regular main sequence star-forming galaxies and starbursts.

evidence.quote: We present a CO(3-2) study of four systems composed of six (ultra) luminous infrared galaxies (U/LIRGs), located at 0.28 $<$ z $<$ 0.44, that straddle the transition region between regular star forming galaxies and starbursts.
We map the distribution of the molecular gas and dust, measure how efficiently they are forming stars, study their dynamics and investigate what triggers star formation.
We obtained Band 6 ALMA observations of CO(3-2) and continuum for CDFS1 (two merging galaxies) using 43 antennas of the 12-m Array (project 2016.1.00896.S, PI: D Rigopoulou).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS$/$JAO.ALMA#2016.1.00896.S.

method.value: Apply a 3sigma cut in each channel of the naturally weighted CO(3-2) cube and integrate across the total line width; apply a 3sigma cut to the continuum map.

evidence.quote: To make the CO(3-2) intensity maps we performed a 3$\sigma$ cut in each channel of the data cube and then integrated the remaining flux across the total width of the emission line. For the continuum 0th moment maps we made a 3$\sigma$ cut on the continuum map.

evidence.quote: In this analysis we assume that the main source of the continuum emission, observed at a rest wavelength $\sim$ 0.9 mm, arises from the Rayleigh-Jeans tail of the dust emission.

evidence.quote: Firstly, we must convert the CO(3-2) flux density from our intensity maps to the integrated line luminosity using the following equation from (cite: solommon_molecular_1997),
To account for metallicity we adopt a metallicity dependent conversion factor described in (cite: genzel_metallicity_2012) and (cite: genzel_combined_2015):

We assume $\alpha_{\rm 0}$ equals the Milky Way conversion factor $\alpha_{\rm MW}$ = 4.36 $\pm$ 0.9 M$_{\odot}$ / (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$), including the correction for Helium, and R$_{1-3}$ = 1.9 ((cite: lamperti_co32co10_2020)), which is a typical value seen in star forming galaxies.

assumptions.value: H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_m = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7; Chabrier (2003) IMF; chi(Z) = 1 for SWIRE7.

evidence.quote: When required, values of H$_{0}$ = 70 km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{m}$ = 0.3 and $\Omega_{\Lambda}$ = 0.7 were used in this paper. When required the initial mass function (IMF) was assumed to be a (cite: chabrier_galactic_2003) form.
For SWIRE7 we set $\chi$(Z) = 1 as it had no \[NII\] 6583 Å detection in PS19.

validation.value: Compare with M14 dust-to-gas ratio alpha_CO estimates and evaluate effect of using local ULIRG alpha_CO = 0.8 or geometric-mean chi(Z).

evidence.quote: If we chose the geometric mean, as in (cite: genzel_combined_2015), then our $\alpha_{\rm{CO (3-2)}}(Z)$ would be $\sim$ 15% higher on average, with a corresponding increase in M$_{\rm mol}$.

Finally, M14 estimated the M$_{\rm mol}$ using the dust to gas mass ratio technique (see M14 and references therein) and inferred an $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ consistent with local star forming galaxies for our sample (with the exception of FLS02), further corroborating our choice.

analysis_steps.goal: Calculate star formation surface densities, molecular gas surface densities, SFE, and depletion times

method.value: Measure star-forming area A_cont from pixels with SNR > 3sigma in continuum map, mask CO(3-2) cube to A_cont and integrate over velocity channels with no threshold, then compute Sigma_mol = M_mol(masked)/A_cont, Sigma_SFR = SFR_IR/A_cont, and tau_dep = 1/SFE.

evidence.quote: we measured this area directly from the moment maps by multiplying the area of each pixel by the number of pixels with SNR
To do this we placed a mask on the emission line cube that ensured only CO(3-2) flux that arises within A$_{\rm cont}$ is extracted.

The surface density for the molecular gas was then calculated using $\Sigma_{\rm mol}$ = M$_{\rm mol}$ / A$_{\rm cont}$ and the SFR surface density was found via $\Sigma_{\rm SFR}$ = SFR$_{\rm IR}$ / A$_{\rm cont}$, where A$_{\rm cont}$ is the area of the star forming region as defined at the start of this section.

key_parameters.value: 3sigma continuum contour mask A_cont; 300 km s^-1 assumed linewidth for SWIRE7 3sigma upper limit

evidence.quote: We assumed a linewidth of 300 km s$^{-1}$ and multiplied the 3$\sigma$/beam by the square root of the number of beams within A$_{\rm cont}$ of SWIRE7 to get the upper limit.

assumptions.value: SFR_IR approximates total SFR; for FLS02-S A_cont equals the CO(3-2) emitting region; for FLS02 system SFR_IR is apportioned between N and S by relative continuum flux; all CDFS1 SFR_IR arises from CDFS1-W.

evidence.quote: For FLS02-S there is a marginal ($\approx$ 4$\sigma$) unresolved continuum detection so we assumed A$_{\rm cont}$ is equal in size to the CO(3-2) emitting region.
Since CDFS1-E is not observed in either continuum or CO(3-2), it is not included in this analysis, and we assume that all the SFR$_{\rm IR}$ arises from CDFS1-W.

For FLS02 we measure the total continuum flux from both sources and find each galaxy’s relative contribution to the total flux. This apportions the SFR$_{\rm IR}$ = 380 M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ for the system into 353 M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ for FLS02-N and 27 M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$ for FLS02-S.

validation.value: Test sensitivity of average tau_dep to using 3sigma/5sigma CO area cuts or total unmasked CO flux within A_cont (changes average tau_dep by < 40 Myr).

evidence.quote: Depending on how we select this larger region, e.g. a 3$\sigma$ or 5$\sigma$ cut on the CO(3-2) maps (which is equivalent to choosing a lower $\sigma$ threshold on the continuum maps), the average $\tau_{\rm dep}$ of our sample only increases by at most 40 Myr and therefore our conclusions remain unchanged.

As a test for this we assumed that the total integrated galaxy flux (see column 3 in Table \[tab:co\]) arises from within A$_{\rm cont}$ and found that the increase in $\Sigma_{\rm mol}$ changes the average $\tau_{\rm dep}$ by less than 40 Myr, demonstrating the robustness of our findings.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit 3D tilted-ring kinematic models to the CO(3-2) data cubes

method.value: Use 3DBAROLO SEARCH algorithm to mask emission and fit a 3D tilted-ring thin-disk model convolved with the synthesized beam to derive v_rot and sigma_gas.

evidence.quote: To fit a kinematic model to the CO(3-2) emission line we used the $^{\rm 3D}$BAROLO code, which fits a 3D tilted ring model to emission line data cubes ((cite: di_teodoro_3d_2015)).
We used the SEARCH algorithm within $^{\rm 3D}$BAROLO to mask the galaxy from the background.

key_parameters.value: SEARCH 5sigma initial cut with 3sigma adjoining threshold; ring width 0.3'' - 0.4''; centre fixed to continuum peak; v_rad = 0; v_sys = 0 at centre; PA and inclination fixed after initial guess; v_rot and sigma_gas free

evidence.quote: The algorithm is a source finder that works by first making a 5$\sigma$ cut across all channels and then assumes that all 3$\sigma$ emission in adjoining channels/pixels are part of the same source ((cite: whitling_duchamp_2012)).

We chose the peak of the continuum as the centre point of each galaxy, set the radial velocity to zero, assumed a thin disk for the scale height, fixed the systematic velocity to zero at the centre of the emission and left the gas surface density to be estimated by the algorithm.

For our ring size we choose 0.3$^{\prime \prime}$ - 0.4$^{\prime \prime}$ to maximize the number of rings when fitting our source, while also ensuring an adequate number of spaxels within each ring to enable an adequate fit.

assumptions.value: Thin disk scale height and zero radial velocity.

evidence.quote: We chose the peak of the continuum as the centre point of each galaxy, set the radial velocity to zero, assumed a thin disk for the scale height, fixed the systematic velocity to zero at the centre of the emission and left the gas surface density to be estimated by the algorithm.

fitting.value: 3D tilted-ring fitting in 3DBAROLO with PA and inclination fixed and v_rot and sigma_gas free.

evidence.quote: We initially let the code make initial guesses for the PA and inclination, and then left them fixed at that value. The v$_{\rm rot}$ and $\sigma_{\rm gas}$ were left as free parameters for the code to fit.

findings_qualitative.value: Transitioning intermediate-z U/LIRGs fall between the loci of main sequence galaxies and starbursts on the Kennicutt-Schmidt relation.

evidence.quote: We detect CO(3-2) emission in four targets and these galaxies fall between the loci of regular star forming galaxies and starbursts on the Kennicutt-Schmidtt relation.

findings_qualitative.value: Intermediate-z cold LIRGs, transitioning U/LIRGs, and warm ULIRGs have similar molecular gas masses, and the increase in L_IR (and SFR) across them is driven by increasing star formation efficiency.

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas and SFR at 0.2 < z < 0.6
evidence.quote: All three samples have similar M$_{\rm mol}$ so the amount of molecular gas available to form stars is not causing the differing L$_{\rm IR}$. When comparing SFE ($\tau_{\rm dep}$) of the three samples it is likely the increase in L$_{\rm IR}$ is being driven by the SFE of the molecular gas.

findings_qualitative.value: All four CO(3-2)-detected targets show signatures of rotating disks and are either in interacting pairs (CDFS1-W, FLS02-N/S) or show morphological/kinematic disturbances (SWIRE5).

evidence.quote: All four galaxies for which we detected a CO(3-2) emission line show signatures of rotating disks. Two of these show ordered rotation (CDFS1-W and SWIRE5) that could be adequately fit with a model rotating gas disk using $^{\rm 3D}$Barolo.

As both FLS02 and CDFS1 are interacting systems and SWIRE5 shows a disturbance that deviates from the disk model, which may be a hidden minor merger or a disk instability, it seems that morphology and kinematics play a significant role in elevating the SFE of a galaxy above the MS.

findings_qualitative.value: SWIRE7 has a strong (~20sigma) continuum detection but no CO(3-2) detection, suggesting either a CO-dark ULIRG, metal-poor ISM with free-free continuum contribution, or an incorrect redshift.

evidence.quote: SWIRE7 poses more of a challenge as it has a strong ($\approx$ 20$\sigma$) detection in the continuum despite having no CO(3-2) detection.

If SWIRE7 is a true CO-dark ULIRG, and not an incorrect redshift, then it poses a challenge to the understanding of the ISM within dusty star forming galaxies galaxies, so followup observations are required.

claims.hypothesis: Intermediate-z U/LIRGs located in the transition region between the main sequence and starbursts in terms of L_IR and dust temperature also bridge the gap between main sequence galaxies and starbursts on the Kennicutt-Schmidt relation.
claims.experiment: Measure spatially resolved CO(3-2) and rest ~0.9 mm continuum with ALMA and NOEMA to derive Sigma_mol, Sigma_SFR, and depletion times tau_dep within the star-forming region A_cont.
claims.result: The four CO(3-2)-detected targets have depletion times of 62 - 301 Myr (average 150 Myr), intermediate between local/intermediate-z starbursting ULIRGs (~10-18 Myr) and regular star-forming/cold LIRG galaxies (~1 Gyr).
claims.finding: Transitioning U/LIRGs populate the intermediate region between regular star-forming galaxies and starbursts on the Kennicutt-Schmidt plane, indicating a gradual change in SFE.

evidence.quote: Our sample of U/LIRGs show a $\tau_{\rm dep}$ of 11 - 301 Myr, with $\tau_{\rm dep}$ of 62 - 301 Myr, excluding SWIRE7 as the source was not detected in the CO(3-2) emission line

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas and SFR at 0.2 < z < 0.6
evidence.quote: These results show that U/LIRGs located in the transition region between starbursts and MS galaxies in terms of dust temperature and L$_{\rm IR}$ also populate the transition region based on SFE, with an average $\tau_{\rm dep}$ of 150 Myr compared to $\tau_{\rm dep}$ $\approx$ 18 Myr for warm ULIRGs and $\approx$ 1 Gyr for cold LIRGs.

claims.hypothesis: Differences in SFR (and L_IR) across intermediate-z U/LIRGs from the upper main sequence to starbursts are driven by star formation efficiency rather than larger molecular gas reservoirs.
claims.experiment: Compare molecular gas masses M_mol and star formation efficiencies of the sample with intermediate-z cold LIRGs (Lee et al. 2017) and warm ULIRGs (Combes et al. 2011).
claims.result: All three samples have similar M_mol budgets, while log(SFE) and log(L_IR) show a strong positive correlation with Pearson's rho = 0.91 (p-value < 0.001).
claims.finding: Increasing SFE, rather than larger molecular gas reservoirs alone, drives the increase in SFR needed to transition a galaxy into the starburst regime at intermediate redshifts.

evidence.quote: Compared to low luminosity LIRGs and high luminosity ULIRGs at similar redshifts, we find they all have similar molecular gas budgets with the difference in their star formation rates (SFR) driven by the star formation efficiency (SFE).

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas and SFR at 0.2 < z < 0.6
evidence.quote: There is a statistically significant strong positive correlation for log(SFE) - log(L$_{\rm IR}$) of the three samples, with a Pearson’s $\rho$ = 0.91 (p-value < 0.001).

claims.hypothesis: Elevated SFE in transitioning intermediate-z U/LIRGs is linked to galaxy interactions and morphological/kinematic disturbances.
claims.experiment: Analyze CO(3-2) and continuum morphologies and fit 3D tilted-ring disk models using 3DBAROLO to the CO(3-2) cubes.
claims.result: CDFS1-W and SWIRE5 are well fit by rotating disks (V_rot = 259 and 346 km s^-1), with CDFS1-W in an early-stage interacting pair and SWIRE5 showing a SE CO/continuum excess and high dispersion; FLS02-N and FLS02-S are an interacting pair with disturbed velocity gradients that cannot be fit by a simple disk.
claims.finding: All four CO-detected galaxies are either in interacting systems or show deviations from an isolated rotating disk, suggesting interaction stage and morphological disturbance elevate SFE above the main sequence.

evidence.quote: In the four targets that have CO(3-2) emission line detections FLS02-N and FLS02-S show signatures of disturbed disks and were unable to be adequately fitted with a $^{\rm 3D}$BAROLO model; whereas CDFS1-W and SWIRE7 show ordered rotation and were fit with a model thin disk.

To conclude, all four galaxies that are observed in CO(3-2) are interacting and/or show deviations from a model isolated disk galaxy, which may explain why their SFE is greater than cold LIRGs at similar redshifts.

why_this_data.value: Targets straddle the transition region between MS LIRGs and starbursting ULIRGs at 0.28 < z < 0.44 and already have Herschel IR, single-dish CO, and optical IFS data; spatially resolved CO(3-2) and ~0.9 mm continuum map the star-forming molecular clouds and obscured star formation.

evidence.quote: In addition, the sample straddles the region between the MS LIRGs and starbursting ULIRGs at this epoch, so it is ideal for investigating the transition between MS and starburst galaxies and its link to interaction stage, and also enabling a better insight into the U/LIRG population at an epoch when the universe is experiencing a decrease in SFRD.

The CO(3-2) transition is 33 K above the ground state and has a critical density of $>$ 10$^{4}$ cm$^{-3}$ at temperatures $<$ 20 K, so it traces the molecular clouds within the ISM from which stars are formed (e.g. (cite: rigby_chimps_2016)), hence these observations allow us to explore the relationship between molecular gas and ongoing star formation.

why_this_method.value: Metallicity-dependent alpha_CO(Z) is chosen because these intermediate-z U/LIRGs have softer radiation fields, different ISM conditions, and earlier interaction stages than local ULIRGs; masking to A_cont ensures maximum spatial overlap between molecular gas and obscured star formation.

evidence.quote: Our sample of U/LIRGs have different ISM conditions compared to those of local ULIRGs (as discussed in M14) and are in an earlier stage of interaction (PS19). Therefore the metallicity dependent $\alpha_{\rm{CO (3-2)}}$(Z) is the most appropriate conversion factor for our sample.
Our motivation for using the A$_{\rm cont}$, i.e. the 3$\sigma$ cut on the continuum, to calculate the surface densities, is to ensure maximum overlap between star forming regions and molecular gas.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using local ULIRG conversion factor alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun / (K km s^-1 pc^2) or the geometric mean of the two Genzel et al. (2015) metallicity scaling functions.

evidence.quote: If we chose the geometric mean, as in (cite: genzel_combined_2015), then our $\alpha_{\rm{CO (3-2)}}(Z)$ would be $\sim$ 15% higher on average, with a corresponding increase in M$_{\rm mol}$.

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas and SFR at 0.2 < z < 0.6
evidence.quote: If we were to use the low-z ULIRG value ($\approx$ 0.8 M$_{\odot}$ / (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^{2}$) for CO(1-0), (cite: downes_rotating_1998)) our $\tau_{\rm dep}$ would be between 2 - 84 Myr (21 - 84 Myr if we remove SWIRE7).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using larger areas based on 3sigma or 5sigma CO(3-2) cuts or using total unmasked CO flux within A_cont when computing surface densities and depletion times.

evidence.quote: Depending on how we select this larger region, e.g. a 3$\sigma$ or 5$\sigma$ cut on the CO(3-2) maps (which is equivalent to choosing a lower $\sigma$ threshold on the continuum maps), the average $\tau_{\rm dep}$ of our sample only increases by at most 40 Myr and therefore our conclusions remain unchanged.

As a test for this we assumed that the total integrated galaxy flux (see column 3 in Table \[tab:co\]) arises from within A$_{\rm cont}$ and found that the increase in $\Sigma_{\rm mol}$ changes the average $\tau_{\rm dep}$ by less than 40 Myr, demonstrating the robustness of our findings.

limitations_admitted.value: AGN contribution to the IR and sub-mm continuum cannot be completely ruled out.

evidence.quote: It is difficult to rule out AGN contribution, but as our sample do not show broad components in the H$\alpha$ emission line (PS19) we assume they are star formation dominated.

limitations_admitted.value: Herschel/SPIRE resolution (~20 arcsec) cannot resolve individual galaxies in the interacting pairs FLS02 (separated by ~4 arcsec) and CDFS1 (~7 arcsec), so L_IR is measured for the combined systems.

evidence.quote: We are, therefore, constrained by the resolution afforded by the Herschel$/$SPIRE bands, which is $\approx$ 20 arcseconds ((cite: griffin_herschel-spire_2010)). Hence, the L$_{\rm IR}$ reported for the two interacting systems, FLS02 (centres separated by $\approx$ 4$^{\prime \prime}$) and CDFS1 (separated by $\approx$ 7$^{\prime \prime}$), corresponds to the entire system and, cannot be calculated for each of the two nuclei independently.

limitations_admitted.value: Small sample size prevents drawing strong conclusions on whether the Kennicutt-Schmidt relation is bimodal or continuous.

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas and SFR at 0.2 < z < 0.6
evidence.quote: As our sample is small we cannot draw any strong conclusions, and expanding the available samples of transitioning objects with future observations is necessary to fully explore this open issue.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial resolution of the NOEMA observations (~3.5 - 5.7 kpc) is insufficient to resolve velocity dispersion profiles in FLS02 or disentangle clumpy disk instabilities from a hidden minor merger in SWIRE5.

evidence.quote: Higher spatial resolution observations are needed to properly probe the velocity structure and determine what is triggering the high rates of SFR.
As the major axis of the synthesized beam is $\approx$ 3.5 kpc in width we require high spatial resolution observations to disentangle the possible scenarios.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only one of the four systems (CDFS1) was observed with ALMA; the other three systems were observed with NOEMA at ~3x coarser angular resolution (~0.8''-1.0'' vs 0.31''), which may systematically affect the measured 3sigma continuum areas A_cont and surface densities.

The strong log(SFE) vs log(L_IR) correlation (rho = 0.91) across the combined literature samples is partly driven by the different alpha_CO assumptions adopted for the different sub-samples (0.8 for Combes et al. warm ULIRGs vs 2.5-6.3 for this work and 4.36 for Lee et al. cold LIRGs).

Note a typo in Section 3.4 where the text states 'CDFS1-W and SWIRE7 show ordered rotation and were fit with a model thin disk' whereas Table 3, Figure 5, and the Conclusion show the fitted target is SWIRE5 (SWIRE7 is undetected in CO).

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data available from the ALMA archive; NOEMA data shared upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.

evidence.quote: The ALMA data underlying this research is available from the ALMA archive. The NOEMA data can be shared upon reasonable request to the corresponding author.

missing_for_reproduction: NOEMA raw/calibrated visibility data (projects W19BV and W20GC are only available upon request, not in a public archive as stated)
Exact continuum map RMS values needed to define the 3sigma contour masks A_cont
Exact velocity integration ranges and line-free channel ranges for each galaxy
Exact 3DBAROLO parameter files (ring radii, number of rings, systemic velocities, and centre pixel coordinates)
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~5-20 GB for the single short (0.2 hr on-source) ALMA Band 6 execution on CDFS1, plus a few GB for the NOEMA uv tables and cubes.
reproducibility.score_reason: The ALMA dataset (2016.1.00896.S) is publicly available and the analytical equations, conversion factors, pixel sizes, channel widths, and 3DBAROLO setup are clearly described, but 3 of the 4 systems rely on non-public NOEMA data and exact continuum RMS values and integration windows are not tabulated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: For the ALMA target CDFS1-W, the archival data (2016.1.00896.S) are public, the reduction and analysis steps (CASA pipeline + UVCONTSUB + TCLEAN natural weighting + moment masking + 3DBAROLO fit) are straightforward, and key numeric outputs (S_CO*dv, M_mol, A_cont, tau_dep, V_rot, sigma_gas) are explicitly tabulated.

Metallicity-dependent CO-to-H2 conversion factor formalism and scaling relation.
Conversion from [NII]/Halpha (N2) ratio to gas-phase oxygen abundance 12 + log(O/H).
Calibration converting total infrared luminosity L_IR to SFR_IR.

Herschel SPIRE-FTS [CII] study of the parent intermediate-z U/LIRG sample.
